messages.subject: Truncation for Multivariate Normal Distribution
parts:
Hello, 

I am working on an IRT model with several indicators. From what I've read I know there can be benefits to pulling the parameters for each indicator from a multivariate normal distribution for example (A_k, B_k) ∼ Multivariate Normal ( mu_k, Sigma_k), for each k indicator (where A_k an B_k are the difficulty and discrimination parameters). At the same time though to identify the IRT I want to constrain B_k > 0.  I cannot figure out though how to go about this in Stan. There seems to be two options.  

1) When I declare the the parameters to constrain B_k > 0. But, I think (and tell me if I am wrong) that since I am pulling them from a multivariate normal I have to declare A_k and B_k as a single vector (Parameters_K). Since this is a single vector I cannot find a way to only constrain part of the vector (just the second value).

2) To use truncation when sampling: multi_normal(mu_k, Sigma_k) T[0,]; But again, it seems that this will apply to both parameters. 

As of now I've been just using the absolute value of the B_k, but that seems like a poor way to accomplish this goal. 

Is there something simple I have been missing? 

Thanks so much for any help, 

Kevin Reuning

On Sunday, November 15, 2015 at 1:43:45 PM UTC-5, Kevin Reuning wrote:
I am working on an IRT model with several indicators. From what I've read I know there can be benefits to pulling the parameters for each indicator from a multivariate normal distribution for example (A_k, B_k) ∼ Multivariate Normal ( mu_k, Sigma_k), for each k indicator (where A_k an B_k are the difficulty and discrimination parameters). At the same time though to identify the IRT I want to constrain B_k > 0.  I cannot figure out though how to go about this in Stan. There seems to be two options.  

1) When I declare the the parameters to constrain B_k > 0. But, I think (and tell me if I am wrong) that since I am pulling them from a multivariate normal I have to declare A_k and B_k as a single vector (Parameters_K). Since this is a single vector I cannot find a way to only constrain part of the vector (just the second value).

You can declare them separately

parameters {
  real A[K];
  real<lower=0> B[K];
}

At this point, you could compose a bivariate normal with truncation as a marginal normal distribution for A[k] times a conditional normal distribution for B[k] given A[k] that is truncated at 0.
2) To use truncation when sampling: multi_normal(mu_k, Sigma_k) T[0,]; But again, it seems that this will apply to both parameters.
Actually, I don't think truncation works for any multivariate density.
As of now I've been just using the absolute value of the B_k, but that seems like a poor way to accomplish this goal.

Yes. Counter productive even because of the bimodality and the confusion it causes to the Hamiltonian when B[k] cross zero.

Ben
